correspondents: Pablo Ariza ("José Mina"), Pedro Duhart, Arturo A. Amaya, Javier Lozano, Charles Moneglia, Manuel de la Hoz ("Manuel Escudero"), Isauro Suárez and others → Félix Díaz and his aliases (José González, R. W. Greer, Pedro Suárez, Guillermo Rosas Jr.)
shelfmark: CEHM-Carso, Fondo DCXXI (Archivo de Félix Díaz): DCXXI.3.231.1 (Duhart, NY 29 Aug 1921, 21 code names), DCXXI.3.242.1 (Amaya, Havana 27 Sep 1921), DCXXI.3.263.1 and 3.278.1 (Mina, 8 and 30 Nov 1921), DCXXI.3.256.2 (2 Nov 1921, signer in code), DCXXI.3.288.1 (Suárez, 17 Dec 1921), DCXXI.3.301.2, DCXXI.3.323.1 (12 Jan 1922), DCXXI.5.474.2 (Lozano, 10 May 1922), DCXXI.5.514.1 (Moneglia, 10 Jun 1922), DCXXI.6.576.1 (25 Aug 1922), DCXXI.7.656.1 (Escudero, 6 Nov 1921)
folio_note: About 12 typed letters, each with a handful of enciphered names or short runs; CEHM marks them Formato Digital (scans exist, viewing needs a CEHM reader account)
status: CEHM catalogue: "incluye claves no descifradas" / "clave sin descifrar" on each record. why: Names of the officers, financiers and agents in the 1921-22 felicista plots against Obregón, which the letters hide on purpose.

title: Captain-general of Cuba (José Cienfuegos) → Marqués de Casa-Irujo, Havana despatch on news from the New York Gazette, in cipher
correspondents: José Cienfuegos Jovellanos, captain-general of Cuba → Carlos Martínez de Irujo, Marqués de Casa-Irujo (Secretary of State)
folio_note: images on PARES; length not known
status: PARES title 'Gobernador Habana sobre noticias de Gaceta de Nueva York', found under 'en cifra' and 'no descifrada'. Galende Díaz (Rev. Complutense de Historia de América 26, 2000, p. 66 n. 52) cites this very document as an example of Cienfuegos's 1817 cipher, which replaces the vowels by digits (A=5, E=3, I=1, O=2, U=4) and keeps the consonants.
